To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MSP was able to detect a cumulative, univariate scale of feeding difficulties in elderly people with a diagnosis of dementia.
the Mokken scaling analysis of feeding difficulty in a psychogeriatrictic setting showed that a cumulative scale exists and that the items of this scale can be used to assess feeding difficulty.

the MSP can be applied to the measurement and interpretation of feeding difficulty in a sample of elderly people with dementia, and that this difficulty increases in a cumulative manner as dementia progresses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the measurement of the degree of difficulty in feeding elderly people with dementia and the demonstration that this method is valid.
the development of a method to measure feeding difficulty in elderly dementia patients, and with the use of this method to investigate the nature of this difficulty.
the application of Mokken Scaling to the measurement of the severity of feeding difficulty in people with dementia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mokken scaling approach to the measurement of obstinacy and passivity in elderly people with severe dementia has some promise.

the Mokken scaling analysis of the feeding difficulty scale in the current work has provided a basis for the further development of this scale as a tool for the clinical assessment of feeding difficulty in dementia.
Mokken scaling is not a panacea for all measurement difficulties but that, in the right circumstances, it can be a useful and valuable tool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MSP is a useful tool in the analysis of data on feeding difficulty in elderly patients with dementia.
the MSP can be used to construct scales from items that measure the same construct and that the scales can be used for the analysis of the pattern of difficulties in feeding.
the MSP is a promising technique for the construction and validation of scales for use in clinical settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mokken scaling is a useful method for analysing data on a small sample.

the Mokken scaling technique is a useful and powerful tool in the analysis of the pattern of difficulty in a set of items, in this case, the feeding difficulty items in the Dutch version of the Nursing Home Minimum Data Set (NHB-MDS).
MSP can be a useful tool to investigate the accumulation of difficulty in feeding elderly people with dementia.
